name: Orbit AI - Phase 6 - Pipeline reporting digest (W6.1)

nodes.name: Every Monday at 6am
nodes.notes: W6.1: 'Pipeline reporting/dashboard... Schedule / on-demand... Auto (internal reporting).' Weekly, not daily - a funnel/revenue digest is meaningfully different week over week; daily would mostly repeat itself. This pass's own judgment call, no cadence given in the source docs for this item. A real 'on-demand' trigger (a Command Center button) isn't built - would need a new Command Center route calling this workflow's webhook equivalent; not built speculatively without a page to put the button on.

nodes.name: Fetch all Opportunities
nodes.notes: Whole-table fetch, not a filtered/paginated query - same 'Twenty CRM's real filter/pagination support isn't confirmed' discipline as ai-activity-summary.workflow.json's own Activity Event fetch. Worth revisiting once Opportunity volume makes a full fetch impractical - not a concern yet with nothing live generating volume.

nodes.name: Fetch LiveClient Companies
nodes.notes: Same query health-scoring.workflow.json and cx-cadence.workflow.json both use - active client count for the digest.

nodes.name: Fetch recent Billing Periods
nodes.notes: Whole-table fetch, filtered client-side (next node) to periods starting in the last 30 days - same reasoning as the Opportunity fetch above.

nodes.name: Compute funnel stats
nodes.notes: The three fetches above run SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel - a deliberate simplification, same reasoning lead-intake-to-demo-dashboard.workflow.json's own notes give for a similar choice: this is a weekly digest, latency doesn't matter, and avoiding a 3-input Merge node (n8n's Merge node parameter shape is already flagged elsewhere in this repo as the single most uncertain node type to import) sidesteps a real correctness risk a naive 3-way parallel fan-in would have had here - each of the three fetch nodes produces exactly one response item, so this node can safely reference each by name with a single .item, no merge needed.

nodes.name: Draft pipeline digest

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-opus-5', max_tokens: 600, system: [{ type: 'text', text: 'You write a short weekly pipeline digest for a sales team, from raw funnel stats (stage counts, active client count, trailing-30-day revenue in cents). Call out anything notable - a stage with an unusually large backlog, low revenue, etc. 3-5 sentences, no preamble, dollar amounts not cents.', cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } }], messages: [{ role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify($json) }] }) }}

nodes.notes: Same model-routing policy every other Claude call in this repo documents (see phase-4-intelligence-layer/README.md): Claude stays the default, no second real caller exists yet to make Gemini/Grok routing a decision with anything to test against.

nodes.name: Post digest
nodes.notes: Routes to #accounting - alertRouting.ts's accounting route extended this pass to match 'pipeline-reporting' alongside 'contract-amendment'/'billing-period'/'refund'. Not a perfect semantic fit (this is funnel activity, not strictly a financial event) but the closest of the 11 LOCKED channel names (05 Section 14) to 'revenue/pipeline visibility' - flagged here rather than inventing a 12th channel outside the brief's own fixed taxonomy.
